title: Fifty Years, One Word Short
concept: On November 10th Alaska's Department of Natural Resources approved a 50-year lease of about 715 acres for STAK Energy's gas-powered data center on the North Slope, case ADL 422741. The notice says data center and high-performance computing and never says AI, the Northern Alaska Environmental Center, an advocacy group, lists artificial intelligence computing among the possible uses. ADN reports 1 to 3 gigawatts, North Slope gas and no Railbelt connection, STAK says no ratepayer impact, World Oil reported a 15-year gas deal, the state got 1,205 comments and ADN says most were opposed, the governor-elect says he would support a moratorium and reconsideration is due November 30th. The film draws all of it on one survey stake tag with a raven as witness, lets the 1,205 comments fall as paper snow onto the line, and ends on a hard cut at the tag with an empty IN RETURN line.

fingerprint.light_story: rose-line dusk, paper-lit cutaways, a hard cut to black
fingerprint.metaphor: a survey stake whose tag the lease, the gas deal and the public each pull on, watched by a raven

palette: lifted dusk dome #1B3A55 under a pale rose horizon line, trampled glacier snow, raven black, parchment #D6C9A8 with charcoal text #1B2230, fluorescent lime survey flagging #B8F23A on the stake tag alone, brick red #C0272D on the crate tabs alone
divergence_note: The last films were pink-gold ice fog with amber (11-11), a violet shore with vermilion and lemon (11-10), an oxblood courtroom (11-09), a permafrost road (11-08), a teal transformer yard (11-07) and a tangerine office (11-06). This film is a lifted blue dusk with a rose horizon line over trampled snow, with fluorescent lime survey flagging on one object (breaking the three-run warm accent streak) and red only on the crate tabs. Its hero is the stake tag with a raven as supporting witness, its device is a clothesline that carries every document, its comments arrive as paper snow, its Test is slips weighing the line down, and it ends on a hard cut with the stake still leaning, no crane-up and no lamp pool. Honest cost: seven of twelve shots stay at the stake and the macro and overhead stages are camera framings of the same pieces.

treatment.title: Fifty Years, One Word Short
treatment.summary: The question the state paperwork raises is about time and words, so the hero is a witness that outlives seasons, a raven, and the throughline is a survey stake tag that the lease, the gas deal and the public each pull on. A neutral animal hero keeps the film from implying an AI the state never wrote. The Mailroom gives the 1,205 comments the longest held scene of the film.

angle.thesis: Alaska approved a 50-year lease for a gas-fired computing campus that powers itself off the Railbelt grid, and the state's own notice never says AI, so the real argument is about land, gas and half a century, and the design only wins if it holds.
angle.falsifiability: False if a primary record (the state notice or a STAK statement) describes the campus as AI, if it ties into the Railbelt grid or lands a cost on ratepayers, or if the lease is undone by reconsideration before November 30th.
supporting_facts: c9 and c10 (state notice: data center, high performance computing)
c32 (notice never uses AI, only Northern Journal says it, c31)
c13 and c15 (off-grid, North Slope gas, per ADN)
c4 and c5 (50 years, about 715 acres)
angle.fair_counterpoint: 1,205 comments, most opposed per ADN (c21, c22), no ratepayer impact is STAK's own claim (c20), and the incoming governor says he would support a moratorium (c27, not tied to STAK). A half century committed on the way out of one administration gets ahead of the public. The explainer must not read as helping the developer reframe the debate.
angle.closing_question: If a project powers itself and never touches the grid, what should Alaska ask of it in return for 50 years of state land?
runner_ups: Pure vocabulary angle (what the notice doesn't say), lost because it risks pedantry
Pure win angle (sell Slope gas), lost because its supports are single-sourced
angle.second_movement: The paperwork says computing, not AI, and the 15-year gas deal World Oil reported is shorter than the 50-year land term.
guardrails: Never say the state or STAK calls it AI
Attribute 1 to 3 GW to ADN, no ratepayer impact to STAK, $500M as an estimate
No Exxon unless attributed to World Oil, no size comparison, gas deal reported not signed
